generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, this means bringing all three together on any group task, whether it is a coaching presentation, a team lab report or a pitch for a club project. You present your own part with authority and defend it when questioned, you listen to the rest of the group and build on their ideas, and you steer any disagreement about the plan. Afterwards you reflect honestly on how the team worked and carry one change into the next piece. Treating these as one practice is what makes you a sport student others want on their side.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two sport students work on the same group presentation about a training programme. Tom prepares his slides but stays silent when the group clashes over the schedule, and afterwards writes only that 'we got there in the end'. Amara presents her section with authority, defends her choice of drills when challenged, listens to a teammate's concern about recovery time and adjusts the plan, then reflects that naming each person's strength early is what calmed the clash. Both knew the programme, but Amara brought authority, collaboration and reflection together on the one task.
generatedProse.summary: Presenting and working with others in sport are most useful as one practice, not three separate skills. On every coaching talk and group project you bring authority, collaboration and reflection together, and carry one change into the next. It is this habit that makes you a sport graduate who leads well and works well with a team.

check.body: In a group presentation, a student owns their section and defends it, listens and adapts with the team, helps steer a disagreement, then reflects honestly afterwards. What does this show?

items.text: Their next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved.
Nothing; feedback comes at the end, so it cannot affect anything that follows.
Only the mark on the first programme, which cannot now change.
The deadline for the next programme.

feedback.correct: That's right. Using the feedback fed back into the next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following programme improved: that is the cycle working.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student changed before the next programme, not the old mark or the deadline.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Using the feedback fed back into the student's next round of learning and preparation, which is why the next programme improved. The old mark cannot change and the deadline is not part of the cycle; feedback is not the end, it feeds the next turn.

_items.text: That the student is using presenting, collaborating and reflecting as one practice of working with people.
_items.feedback: Yes. All three are there, working together on the same piece of work.

_items.text: That the student is doing more than any one piece of group work really needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each part does a different job, and together they make the work stronger.

_items.text: That only the reflection at the end really mattered.
_items.feedback: Not so. The authority and collaboration did the real work, and reflection improves the next round.

_items.text: That presenting and collaborating are the same thing.
_items.feedback: They are different parts of the one practice, used together rather than merged.
